item.title: Re: About all the "Should Be Main SCP" stuff
item.content:encoded:
I'm not saying your opinion or view is invalid, but you're pretty much the only person I've ever interacted with that treated Jabberwocky - or its Kingdom of Loathing familiar which I'm more familiar with - as a serious piece. Hell, Wikipedia defines it as a "The playful, whimsical poem".

I do imagine the thought process of a researcher dealing with 4237-J. They struggle to find the right words, get a bit frustrated, make jibberish words, re-read them, and laugh, because these researchers have been 'taught' by the Foundation to write very clinically, unemotionally, and logically… and the nonsense they write is the clincal, unemotional, and logical way for the object. If this SCP had background music during the tests, this would play.

item.title: Re: About all the "Should Be Main SCP" stuff
item.content:encoded:
Just adding in inventive words doesn't make the subject inherently humorous; look at Jabberwocky as an example. Readers tend to initially smile and chuckle, but after the initial laughs, it stops being viewed as a humor piece and ends up taken much more seriously. It's even introduced words to the English language, with vorpal and chortle both being invented whole cloth. Beneath the surface humor is a serious piece, and this is much the same.

Creepy Objects What Muck With Perceptions are well represented on the main list because they are disturbing. There's a reason that I Am A Toaster is the fifth highest rated article on the site and 055 is the twelfth—cognitohazards that screw with sense of self and the ability to interact with them are terrifying. Imagine the thought process of a researcher that is familiar with the effects of 4237-J who interacts with it, and then has to try and describe the event. Imagine yourself as that researcher, unable to even think about your recent actions in a way that makes sense.

That sense of unease versus made up words, it's just not a contest. It's a stronger main article listing than -J.

item.title: About all the "Should Be Main SCP" stuff
item.content:encoded:
I had a lot of people say this about The Grim Bucket, and like it, I don't see this one as a 'normal' SCP.

Maybe it's because I haven't done the testing log yet (which, in-character, I'll be able to Joss the 'words no longer exist' angle; I'm very good at using odd not-really-made-up words to describe things), but like the Grim Bucket, I feel there is an inherent lightheartedness to the thing. I'd say we have enough Creepy Objects That Muck With Its Perception in the main SCP. 4237 might be, on its edges and fridge logic be creepy… but I see 4237 as a generally harmless and fun object. No matter what's causing it, the idea that these stuffy, write-clinically-at-all-times people are essentially 'forced' to write in babble that they actively stamp out elsewhere is hilarious to me.

I''ll open this up to others with a Testing Log… somewhat soon. I'm just intoxicated that I don't feel comfortable starting a new page.

item.content:encoded:
Actually, my concept of it is that you do realize it makes no rational sense, but it's the only way to get the idea out. Something about 4237 makes people unable to assign real words to what it does. Let's say you were immune to 4237's effects, and you dropped it. You'd say you just dropped it, and that it bounced. But for everyone else, saying "it fell and bounced" isn't correct enough to say that. 'Fell' and 'bounced' aren't right enough. It's something different, what it did was… um… christ, it was like, it… fuck it, it swoomed down and boingboinged. Remember, every written / typed report for 4237 has had all of its "um, fuck, it's like, um" stuff removed. Which is a lot.

Ever have a situation where you're telling someone a story, get stuck on a word, and it sorta kills the exchange because every suggestion your friend makes is wrong? That's this thing.

I'm not sure how this thing will go over. It seems like an idea joke SCP in which people think up a series of Things It Does, then goes about making up words and analogies in order to mask what exactly is going on. Plus, it's a take-that at how SCPs are supposed to be written very clearly and plainly, without anything that 4237 can't be described without. But since I don't know it's going to be received, I'm not gonna add a Testing Log for other people just yet.

Oh yeah, and a Truncated Icosidodecahedron? I picked it cuz it's a Long Ass Word and, based on images I've seen, has a visual unease that I felt matched up with the SCP's inability to be explained.
